headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI can expose workspace content to vendor backends, while PaddleOCR can process documents/images; other pairwise risks are limited by lack of shared write channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists only if Notion AI content is manually copied into PaddleOCR or a shared workspace is used as an intermediary. Notion AI is vendor-hosted and PaddleOCR is a document processor, but neither profile shows a direct shared channel or permissive parser by default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Notion-generated text into PaddleOCR inputs without review, prompt-like instructions can propagate.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or file handoff, injected content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Review any Notion-generated text before sending it to PaddleOCR.
Use a plain-text handoff template that strips instructions.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any automation that forwards AI output directly into OCR pipelines.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its vendor-hosted backend can receive those contents. PaddleOCR processes documents and images, so if the same sensitive files are routed through both, leakage can occur in default workflows. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the same sensitive document is opened in Notion AI and then sent to PaddleOCR, both services will see it.
IF workspace pages contain secrets or regulated data, Notion AI's vendor backend receives that content.
mitigations: Exclude secrets and regulated data from Notion pages used with AI.
Redact documents before OCR processing.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive material.
Turn off any automatic document forwarding between the tools.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no evidence of overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem and PaddleOCR only shows API access plus browser use, so direct write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty is limited, but the lack of shared writable surfaces keeps this low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory or database, conflicts can arise.
IF a shared API target is introduced, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only unless a write is necessary.
Assign separate output directories.
Add a simple lock or queue around shared resources.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same document set.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading error is plausible if Notion AI output is treated as authoritative and then fed into PaddleOCR-driven document workflows without verification. Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, while PaddleOCR performs document processing; the pair can therefore amplify mistaken text into downstream actions or records.
conditions: IF Notion AI output is copied into a document that PaddleOCR later parses, errors can propagate.
IF downstream automation trusts OCR-extracted text without human review, incorrect content can be acted on.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use.
Compare OCR output against the source document.
Mark AI-generated text clearly in the workflow.
Block automatic action-taking from OCR results.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to vendor backends, while PaddleOCR can process documents and images under a separate open-source stack. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through both, retention and jurisdictional controls may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are processed through both tools, residency and retention obligations must be checked.
IF the operator relies on different retention policies for the same data class, compliance gaps can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of non-approved workflows.
Document retention settings for both tools.
Route residency-bound data only through approved systems.
Add a quick compliance checklist before processing sensitive documents.
